method: Static independent caller/consumer/guard inspection; no runtime or destructive PoCs

findings.title: Memory JSON truncates in place
source_checks: crystallize_session reads project/ghost/system and calls _write_json at 113,129,156; CLI calls crystallize_session at177.
_write_json uses open(path,"w") followed by f.write with no temporary rename/fsync/recovery.
findings.counterexample: Process interruption after truncation but before complete write destroys prior JSON; next startup cannot recover from this module.
assumptions: Memory topology exists; writer is invoked.
findings.limits: Static persistence bug; no crash PoC or disk durability test.

findings.title: Malformed CRL file falls back to filename literal
source_checks: parse_crl_arg catches every file decode/read exception then splits the filename string (78–81).
main passes that list directly to verify_compliance_certificate (125–130).
standalone_verify rejects only cert_id in crl at713; no later CRL load guard.
findings.counterexample: Existing CRL file becomes invalid JSON; revoked certificate ID does not equal path literal and passes the revocation check if other checks pass.
assumptions: Verifier is run with --cert and --crl; certificate otherwise valid and unexpired.
findings.limits: No forgery claim; caller-supplied CRL must be reliably parsed.

findings.title: JSON ledger hashes are trusted without binding event fields
source_checks: Returns integrity_verified=True and verified=True on matching Merkle root (508–515).
verify_compliance_certificate passes signed expected root to verify_offline_evidence and accepts verified at728–739.
findings.counterexample: Alter payload fields of an event dictionary while retaining its entry_hash; leaves and signed-root comparison remain unchanged.
assumptions: JSON ledger includes event payloads and entry_hash values; certificate/root is otherwise valid.
findings.limits: Hash-only manifests may legitimately attest hashes alone; vulnerability is claiming event integrity for event dictionaries without recomputation.

findings.title: Revocation and dependency validation are separated from insertion
source_checks: add_record checks ACTIVE parent then commits at468.
Ledger append happens outside that transaction, insertion opens a new BEGIN IMMEDIATE at496.
revoke_record calculates closure and commits at632–638; final update opens another transaction at666.
_get_connection creates independent SQLite connections; FULL durability and foreign keys do not recheck parent status.
findings.counterexample: A validates active parent and releases transaction; B revokes parent and computes closure without not-yet-inserted A child; A inserts child with ACTIVE initial status.
assumptions: Concurrent legitimate add_record and revoke_record callers for same dependency graph.
findings.limits: No production API authorization bypass asserted; class concurrency/state invariant defect.

findings.title: Compiler stack frame is fixed despite unbounded spills
source_checks: get_offset starts16 and advances8 for every new Reg, without bound.
compile reserves256 bytes then emits sys_alloc/sys_free calls.
32nd distinct Reg has offset264, equal to call return slot at rsp-8 for aligned rbp.
Targeted consumer search found only public module export in src/lib.rs, no repository executable caller.
findings.counterexample: Generate >31 live spill slots then call sys_alloc/sys_free; call return address overwrites a spill at264, corrupting generated-program value.
assumptions: Caller uses exposed X86Backend.compile with sufficiently large valid IR and executes emitted assembly.
findings.limits: Compiler output defect confirmed statically; deployed consumer/executed exploit not established. P2 matches demonstrated scope.
